text:
Wading through the thick muck and mire of the Fenlands, the baughur looks to be nothing less than a small fleshy island when 
breaching the water. Flies and birds orbit its thick hide as it shovels its tusked face into the thick sediment, its prehensile snout seeking 
out aquatic root vegetables. Often quite calm and docile when in their dozens-strong drove of close kin, the baughur will attempt to 
sink to the bottom of the marsh when confronted by any terrestrial creature threat. Only resorting to violence with their goring tusks 
when protecting their young or spotting their most hated rivals in the Fenlands, the pebbleback auhk. Often standing their ground 
with a display of loud splashes and deep-barreled chest grunts.

Encountering Loud snorts and gargled underwater bellows 
announce the presence of a herd of baughur long before they 
can be seen. Upon approaching the semi aquatic mammals, they 
are usually quite peaceful if met with calm, quiet movements. If 
the smell of blood begins to permeate the surrounding area, or 
they hear overly loud noises, they will quickly flee to safer areas, 
goring and stampeding any that stand in their way.
Defensive Instinct (1/Day) When a friendly baughur it can hear within 
60 ft. of it is slain.
